text.p: Xenova Group Plc on Tuesday became the latest British biotech company to turn to the market for cash, saying it was confident of success despite sticky market conditions in the sector.
Slough-based Xenova, already listed on the U.S. Nasdaq exchange, is hoping to raise 25 million pounds ($38.94 million) through a full listing on the London Stock Exchange.

Xenova chief financial officer Trevor Twose said the timing of a listing had been dictated by the need to fund development of its leading cancer and cardiovascular compounds. They include a cancer drug about to enter intermediate-stage clinical trials.

"We need to put some funding in place and our view was that it is the right time to tackle our home market," said Twose. "It is my belief that the projects have reached a stage where they will produce a flow of news, and that was an important consideration."
Twose said Xenova hopes to publish its pathfinder prospectus early in October and complete the placing "before mid-November."

The move comes at a tricky time for the biotech sector. A string of successful floats, rights issues and placings earlier in the year ended in tears in July when plans by tiny Cambridge-based Cambrio to raise 10 million pounds through a stock market listing were abandoned for lack of support.
More significantly, a 143 million pound rights issue by sector leader British Biotech Plc the same month had to be rescued by underwriters after being only 49 per cent subscribed.
Sharp falls in share prices across the board over the past three months, following 18 months of spectacular gains, have left many investors nursing paper losses and wary.

"People will be reluctant to be pushing more money after bad," said one analyst currently working on another placing, who asked not to be named. "The mood of investors is towards lower risk companies, and obviously lower returns, and that is a move away from early stage drug discovery companies."

Valerie Marshall, a director of Greig Middleton & Co Ltd which is sponsoring the placing, said: "We see this as being very different from some companies that have been out to raise money recently. It is a well-established company which has a portfolio of products, and it is already quoted on Nasdaq."
Xenova raised $32 milllion through its Nasdaq listing in 1992, and is currently capitalised at around $47 million.
Robin Gilbert, an analyst at Panmure Gordon, said the company's cancer drugs, which Xenova hopes will tackle a range of cancers resistant to existing drugs, "look interesting."
The company has also received a vote of confidence from two major drugs players, forming research collaborations with the Parke-Davis arm of Warner-Lambert Co and Japan's Suntory Ltd.
"It is regarded from a scientific point of view reasonably positively," Gilbert said. "The market is not as easy as it was, (but) there must be a chance it will be all right." ($1=.6420 Pound)
